product.name: @nymrel/machine-trust
product.description: A TypeScript library and CLI that generates and audits machine-readable web evidence.

features: Schema.org JSON-LD generation from explicit entity relationships

faqs.question: What does Machine Trust inspect?
faqs.answer: It checks structured data, machine-readable indexes, crawler rules, answer-first summaries, and rendered-copy parity against the configuration supplied by the operator.

faqs.question: Does Machine Trust invent an ownership hierarchy?
faqs.answer: No. Generic sites receive no corporate parent. Explicit caller-supplied relationships are validated, and built or partner properties may credit Nymrel by canonical creator reference.

llmsTxt.title: Nymrel Machine Trust
llmsTxt.summary: Machine Trust generates and audits machine-readable web evidence without inventing ownership, performance, or discovery outcomes.

sections.title: Core modules
sections.description: Generators and validators for inspectable web evidence.

links.title: JSON-LD generator
links.description: Builds Schema.org graphs from explicit configuration and canonical creator references.

links.title: Machine index generator
links.description: Creates token-budgeted llms.txt and llms-full.txt files.

links.title: Crawler policy generator
links.description: Creates declared crawler rules that remain subject to each crawler's behavior.

links.title: DOM parity validator
links.description: Reports observable differences between configured structured data and supplied HTML.

answerFirst.summary: Nymrel Machine Trust is a TypeScript library and CLI for generating structured data, machine-readable indexes, and declared crawler rules, then checking those artifacts against supplied configuration and rendered HTML. Its reports describe observable evidence and limitations; they do not promise rankings, traffic, citations, recommendations, or revenue.
keyTakeaways: Entity relationships come only from explicit configuration
Nymrel attribution uses a canonical creator reference
Fixed timestamps make audit scorecards reproducible
Reports describe eligibility and consistency rather than discovery outcomes
